prompt: On a blocking TCP socket with no local receive shutdown, recv(4096) returns b"" after all preceding data has been consumed. What does this indicate?

options.text: No data has arrived yet; call recv() again shortly
options.explanation: A blocking recv() waits until data arrives; it never returns empty just because nothing is there yet. (A non-blocking socket raises BlockingIOError instead.)

options.text: The peer has closed its sending side (sent FIN); there will be no more data
options.explanation: Correct. An empty read is end-of-stream. Your code should stop reading and, usually, close the socket.
An RST surfaces as an exception, ConnectionResetError, not as an empty read.
A full buffer means there's plenty to read; recv() would return data immediately.

workedExample: For this positive-length read, an empty result indicates end of the peer’s sending stream. Stop waiting for further input. A half-closed connection may still be usable for sending a response; then close or shut down according to the protocol. Forgetting EOF handling can create a busy loop, but the exact TCP state also depends on local shutdown history.
